page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.metal-48xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores utilizing the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it bundles a massive 120,000 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 300 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark physics tests. Its memory subsystem achieves top-tier read and write bandwidth, with uncached large-block reads reaching 897.06 GB/sec. Database and caching performance are highly competitive, with Redis SET operations achieving 378.59 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring in the top 10%. However, single-core performance is moderate, falling into the middle 50% across Geekbench and stress-ng single-core tests, and LLM text generation performance is poor.

Given its bare-metal architecture, massive 120 TB NVMe storage capacity, and high-density DDR5 memory, the i8ge.metal-48xl offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for large-scale, I/O-intensive deployments. The lack of hyperthreading means each of the 192 cores is fully dedicated, avoiding resource contention. This hardware profile is highly suited for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, high-throughput Redis caching layers, data warehousing, and high-volume static web serving.
